Caching in practice

A cache trades memory for latency. This article covers the three patterns that matter most in day-to-day services, and when each one is the right choice for a read-heavy path.

Cache-aside

The application checks the cache first and loads from the database on a miss.

  • Simple to reason about
  • Stale data is possible until the TTL expires

Write-through

Every write goes to the cache and the database together, so reads stay fresh.
